data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Australia factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Australia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time. PISA 2022 used two hour-long subject tests with different students receiving different test questions and subject combinations, plus a student background questionnaire and a school principal questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and comparisons to the OECD average and selected comparison countries. It also highlights subgroup patterns within Australia, including socioeconomic divides (ESCS quintiles), gender differences, and immigrant background differences, and provides contextual indicators on school belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. A key limitation noted is that Australia’s student response rate fell below PISA technical standards, which may introduce a small residual upward bias; the factsheet also flags that some countries/economies with sampling-standard issues require caution.
